extractedBy: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), agent pack POC session
notes: The Button page is a hand-built page (not ComponentGuideTemplate); its copy was read from the rendered sections. Its Sources note says jfs-components 0.1.60, checked 13 September 2026, and the shared evidence file (button-and-layout.md) records almost nothing about Button's own behaviour, so most facts stay at source types. The guide names no other component to use instead.

useWhen.text: One clear action moves someone forward, confirms a choice, or completes a task.

from.quote: Use Button when one clear action moves someone forward, confirms a choice, or completes a task.

avoidWhen.text: Avoid loading as a substitute for transaction progress; it is for while required content is being prepared.

from.quote: Use loading while required content is being prepared, not as a substitute for transaction progress.

absolute.reason: "required" describes the content being prepared, not a constraint on the rule.

anatomy.holds: Holds the action and resolves its visual treatment.

from.quote: Holds the action and resolves its visual treatment.

anatomy.holds: Optional leading node: an icon that clarifies the action.

from.quote: Optional. Use for an icon that clarifies the action.

anatomy.holds: The label: names the outcome in one to three words.

from.quote: Required. Name the outcome in one to three words.

anatomy.holds: Optional icon after the label, for direction or continuation.

from.quote: Optional. Use when direction or continuation matters.

placementAdvice.text: Place the action where the decision happens, and let surrounding content explain the choice.

from.quote: Use surrounding content to explain the choice. Let the button stay concise.

placementAdvice.text: In a wide container, keep the action close to the content it completes.

from.quote: Keep the action close to the content it completes.

placementAdvice.text: Make one action the strongest; competing actions should not share equal emphasis.

from.quote: Two dominant actions make the choice harder to read.

placementAdvice.text: Let container width resolve the layout: the same action can fill a narrow container's width. There is no separate desktop or mobile Button.

from.quote: Container width resolves the layout. Designers choose the label, hierarchy, and size—not a separate “desktop” or “mobile” Button.

configuration.text: Use type default for most actions; it hugs its label or fills its container when the layout asks it to.

from.quote: The standard solid action. It hugs its label or fills its container when the layout asks it to.

configuration.text: Use type fixed for aligned, bounded actions: it keeps long content within the system width limit.

from.quote: Keeps long content within the system width limit. It remains responsive rather than using a hand-set pixel width.

configuration.text: Do not use type fixed for a full-width action: fixed is bounded by the system and will not fill. Use type default for a footer action that fills its container.

from.quote: Fixed is bounded by the system and will not behave like Fill.

configuration.text: Use type glass only over a meaningful backdrop such as rich media or a coloured surface.

from.quote: Use only over a meaningful backdrop

absolute.reason: the line is a short card caption under the Glass example; it is unclear whether it is a hard limit or advice, and the guide does not define a meaningful backdrop.

configuration.text: Do not place type glass on a plain, low-contrast surface: it loses its purpose and can become hard to read.

from.quote: The treatment loses its purpose and can become hard to read.

configuration.text: Appearance identifies the family; Emphasis sets how loudly the action speaks within it.

from.quote: Appearance identifies the family. Emphasis decides how loudly the action speaks within that family.

configuration.text: Reserve Semantic Intent System (AppearanceSystem positive, warning or negative) for an outcome with clear positive, warning or negative meaning.

from.quote: Reserve these appearances for an outcome with clear positive, warning, or negative meaning.

configuration.text: Button / Size M: the action leads a screen, sheet or key step.

from.quote: The action leads a screen, sheet, or key step.

configuration.text: Button / Size S: the action sits inside a card or compact group.

from.quote: The action sits inside a card or compact group.

configuration.text: Button / Size XS: space is dense and the surrounding touch area stays usable.

from.quote: Space is dense and the surrounding touch area stays usable.

configuration.text: Most actions need at most one of the start slot and end icon, and many need neither.

from.quote: Most actions need one at most, and many need neither.

configuration.text: Give disabled a clear condition; hover and pressed happen automatically and are not configured.

from.quote: Hover and pressed happen automatically. Disabled should have a clear condition.

rules.text: Make the action clear before choosing its appearance; the label should explain what happens next.

from.quote: Make the action clear before choosing its appearance. The label should explain what happens next.

rules.text: Lead with a verb, such as “Save details”, “Transfer money” or “View statement”.

from.quote: Use clear actions such as “Save details”, “Transfer money”, or “View statement”.

rules.text: Aim for one to three words. Put the explanation beside the button, not inside it.

from.quote: Aim for one to three words. Put explanation beside the button, not inside it.

rules.text: Add an icon only when it improves recognition, direction, or the action's meaning.

from.quote: Add one only when it improves recognition, direction, or the action’s meaning.

absolute.reason: "only when it improves recognition" is a judgement call; it limits icons to a purpose rather than stating a checkable constraint.

rules.text: Be specific: prefer “Pay ₹500” or “Download report” over a vague “OK” when the outcome can be named.

from.quote: Prefer “Pay ₹500” or “Download report” over a vague “OK” when the outcome can be named.

bad: Click here to transfer your money now

from.quote: Ready for action.

states.when: Appears automatically under a pointer; not configured.

from.quote: Appears automatically under a pointer.

states.when: Appears while the action is held; not configured.

from.quote: Appears while the action is held.

states.when: disabled is true; unavailable until a condition is met.

from.quote: Unavailable until a condition is met.

states.when: loading is true while required content is being prepared; a shape-preserving skeleton holds the action's place.

from.quote: A shape-preserving skeleton holds the action’s place.

from.quote: Write a short, verb-led label
